---
title: "The book: try every feature"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = FALSE)
```

hovercraft ships a Shiny app, the book, with every feature of the package on one page, so you can rest a pointer on a tip
before you write a line of code.

```{r}
hovercraft::hovercraft_book()
```

It needs an interactive R session and the suggested packages shiny and bslib. The table sections also need `DT` or
`reactable`.

## What a section gives you

Each section is one feature, and has five things:

- a live figure: rest the pointer on it, or tab to it
- a line of choices that change the figure
- the R code that draws what you see, ready to copy (the code shown is the code that runs)
- a short list of what to test
- the Shiny inputs your server would get, updated as you act

## The six parts

1. Getting started: one tip, and where it opens.
2. Content: what a tip says, with templates, and the reason a control is off.
3. Interaction: pins, the long form, and what your server hears.
4. Look: presets, size, your own colours and the marks that show a tip is there.
5. From Shiny: tips your server opens, changes and fills with live outputs.
6. Tables: tips on the rows, cells and headers of `DT` and `reactable` tables.

The index has a search box. Type a function or an argument, such as `tip_more` or `max_pins`, and it shows the sections
that use it.

## Start where you need to

Open the book on one section:

```{r}
hovercraft::hovercraft_book(section = "pins")
```

The sections, by part:

- Getting started: `"start"`, `"placement"`
- Content: `"templates"`, `"disabled"` (`when_disabled`)
- Interaction: `"pins"`, `"pin_limits"`, `"more"`, `"more_button"`, `"inputs"`, `"words"` (`labels`)
- Look: `"looks"`, `"size"`, `"colours"`, `"markers"`
- From Shiny: `"server"`, `"output"`
- Tables: `"tables"`, `"columns"`, `"table_pins"`, `"in_place"`, `"table_server"`

## The checklist

Press `C` in the book, or open it with `checklist = TRUE`, and a short checklist shows one test step at a time. A step
ticks when the server gets the input that proves it: pin a tip and the "pin" step is done. It is the quickest way to see
that a feature does what its help page says, .

```{r}
hovercraft::hovercraft_book(section = "pins", checklist = TRUE)
```

## Where to read more

The articles explain how the features fit together: [Get started](hovercraft.html), [Tips in a Shiny app](shiny.html),
[Tips on tables](tables.html), [A short tip with a long form](long-form.html) and [Themes and looks](themes.html). The
[reference](../reference/index.html) says exactly what every argument takes.

`hovercraft_book()` is experimental: its sections may move before a later release.
